0e4caecb0c32c66e4af751b48bfe683e951501d6.summary: Malpedia profile of BlackCat, also called ALPHV or Noberus: a Rust ransomware family sold as ransomware-as-a-service. It runs on Windows, Linux (Debian, Ubuntu, ReadyNAS, Synology) and VMware ESXi. It can encrypt files with AES or ChaCha20, delete volume shadow copies, stop processes, services and ESXi virtual machines, and spread using PsExec. The page says it has been seen in attacks since November 18, 2021. Listed actors are Alpha Spider, RansomHub and Vanilla Tempest. Most of the page is a reference list of vendor and government reports.

0e7aa3afb4a262f43d979753d190bf8c19d8a9e7.summary: Splunk Threat Research Team blog dated November 11, 2021 (part 1 of 2) on FIN7 tools: the JSS Loader and Remcos. It describes JavaScript first-stage delivery through spear-phishing, WMI-based host information gathering, data exfiltration to C2 over HTTP POST and DNS, screenshot capture and browser database parsing, and lists detection content. The report leaves open whether the resurfaced JSS Loader activity is a splinter group, a copycat, or FIN7 itself. The report cites the US Department of Justice for about 15 million cards stolen in the United States.
